title: Prefill-Decode Aggregation or Disaggregation? Unifying Both for Goodput-Optimized LLM Serving (TaiChi)
technique: unified PD aggregation/disaggregation with P-heavy and D-heavy instances; sliders for instance ratio and chunk sizes; latency shifting via flowing decode scheduling and length-aware prefill scheduling

optimized_metrics.evidence: To support balanced TTFT and TPOT SLOs and maximize goodput, TaiChi introduces hybrid-mode inference
TaiChi maximizes the number of SLO-satisfied requests
Goodput denotes the maximum request rate that can be sustained while meeting SLO targets; SLO bounds on TTFT and TPOT
optimized_metrics.stat_quote: Following prior work [36], we evaluate all methods based on the maximum achievable goodput under the 90% SLO attainment rate; Latency SLOs specify bounds on TTFT and TPOT

optimized_metrics.evidence: Latency service-level objectives (SLOs) quantify user-perceived performance by specifying bounds on time-to-first-token (TTFT) and time-per-output-token (TPOT)
optimized_metrics.stat_quote: Following prior work [36], we evaluate all methods based on the maximum achievable goodput under the 90% SLO attainment rate; Latency SLOs specify bounds on TTFT and TPOT

headline_claim.text: TaiChi improves goodput by up to 77% compared to state-of-the-art systems under balanced TTFT and TPOT SLOs

metric_definitions.definition_quote: TTFT measures the latency from request arrival to the first token, primarily determined by prefill time
metric_definitions.notes: from arrival, so includes queueing; paper also shows queuing dominates TTFT in PD disaggregation (Fig 7)

metric_definitions.definition_quote: TPOT reflects the average per-token latency during decode
Goodput denotes the maximum request rate that can be sustained while meeting SLO targets [36].
metric_definitions.notes: request-rate based (req/s), DistServe-style; both TTFT and TPOT must be met per request

metric_definitions.term_as_written: maximum achievable goodput under the 90% SLO attainment rate
metric_definitions.definition_quote: Following prior work [36], we evaluate all methods based on the maximum achievable goodput under the 90% SLO attainment rate

slo_spec: Two balanced SLO configs per workload (Table 3, TTFT,TPOT): ShareGPT (3s,110ms) and (4s,70ms); Arxiv summarization (4s,70ms) and (6s,50ms) (cell-to-SLO1/SLO2 mapping read from garbled table extraction). Qwen2.5-32B TPOT relaxed by 10 ms. Motivation experiments: relaxed TTFT 16s/tight TPOT 60ms; tight TTFT 5s/relaxed TPOT 250ms; balanced TTFT 6s/TPOT 100ms. Goodput at 90% attainment.
tradeoff_acknowledged: TTFT-vs-TPOT tradeoff between PD aggregation and disaggregation; latency shifting deliberately degrades TTFT/TPOT of requests that already meet SLOs to protect at-risk ones
hardware: 8x A100-80GB NVLink (real); 4-node 8-GPU A100 DGX cluster simulated with Vidur for motivation
extractor_notes: Uses Vidur for the motivation study. Goodput is a rate at 90% attainment of the joint TTFT+TPOT SLO; latency reductions (TTFT 13.2x, TPOT 1.69x) reported at P90 at TaiChi's max goodput. Explicit 'latency shifting' = intentionally trading away per-request slack.
load_class_quote: we simulate request arrivals using a Poisson process with varying rates, as in prior work [3, 36]
